procedures.title: Share free/busy between the target and a source
procedures.goal: Users of the target and of the source see each other's availability during the migration, through the Microsoft 365 cross-tenant access policy, which is removed at closure.
prerequisites: The partner configuration exists in both tenants.
The Microsoft 365 policy has rolled out to both tenants: rollout goes tenant by tenant, see the Message center.
Policy.ReadWrite.CrossTenantAccess and Policy.ReadWrite.CrossTenantCapability permissions, or the Global Administrator role.
The customer approved the level of calendar detail.

steps.command: Get-OrganizationRelationship | Format-List Name, DomainNames, Enabled, FreeBusyAccessEnabled, FreeBusyAccessLevel

steps.text: In each tenant, open the Microsoft 365 trust to the other tenant. The policy is inbound, so both sides must create it.
steps.command: Update-MgPolicyCrossTenantAccessPolicyPartner -CrossTenantAccessPolicyConfigurationPartnerTenantId <partner id> -BodyParameter @{ m365CollaborationInbound = @{ users = @{ accessType = 'allowed'; targets = @(@{ target = 'AllUsers'; targetType = 'user' }) } } }

steps.text: In each tenant, allow the availability capability. crossTenantCalendarAvailabilityBasic replaces AvailabilityOnly, and crossTenantCalendarAvailabilityLimitedDetails replaces LimitedDetails.
Turn off the existing relationships between these tenants, in both tenants at the same time: they take priority over the capability.
Test both ways with the meeting Scheduling Assistant.
At closure, remove the capabilities and relationships that are no longer needed, in both tenants.

An account in each tenant sees the availability of the other.
risks: LimitedDetails exposes the subject and location of appointments. Have this level approved.
A relationship left active takes priority over the capability and stops working when EWS is turned off.
Until the policy has rolled out to a tenant, keep its relationship: turn it off only once the capability is in place.

procedures.title: Settle matching shared mailboxes
procedures.goal: Each shared or resource mailbox of a source that has a match in the target is merged or kept separate, as the customer decides.

The customer owner of each mailbox is known.
The identity matrix of the source is in progress.

steps.text: List the shared mailboxes of the target to confirm each pair.
steps.command: Get-Mailbox -RecipientTypeDetails SharedMailbox -ResultSize Unlimited | Select-Object DisplayName, Alias, PrimarySmtpAddress, UserPrincipalName, IsDirSynced

steps.text: Have the customer decide each pair: merge or keep separate.
For a merge, set Type to Shared and Decision to Duplicate. Put the UPN of the target mailbox in Target UPN, not only its SMTP address.

For a synced mailbox (IsDirSynced is True), add the address in on-premises Active Directory, because Exchange attributes are still managed there.
Changing the alias does not change the SMTP address.
A shared mailbox over 50 GB needs an Exchange Online Plan 2 license.

procedures.title: Lower the record TTL to 300 s

The pilot validated that the copy tool carries terms over.

steps.text: List the term groups of the source and the target, to spot conflicts.
Prefer the copy tool, if the pilot confirms that it keeps the IDs.
Otherwise, export each term group of the source.
Import the file into the target, before any content copy.
Check the IDs on a sample, then test a metadata column on a pilot site.
steps.where: SharePoint admin center > Term store, target tenant

verification: Get-PnPTermSet -TermGroup '<group>' | Format-Table Name,Id shows the same IDs as the source.
risks: Without the same IDs, copied metadata columns lose their link to the terms.
A group with the same name in the target can conflict. Rename or prefix it before the import.
Whether the PnP import keeps IDs must be confirmed during the pilot.

procedures.title: Prepare the addresses of the synced target accounts
procedures.goal: Each target account synced from on-premises Active Directory receives the addresses of the source, without going through Exchange Online.
prerequisites: The matrix is validated: the Duplicate rows name the target account to keep.
Access to on-premises Active Directory of the target and to the Entra Connect server.
The technical team chose the method.

steps.text: Confirm that the account is synced. Exchange Online then refuses Set-Mailbox -EmailAddresses.

Test the case during the pilot on one account, then choose the method: add the address on-premises (below), or move Exchange attributes to cloud management. The second method applies to the accounts concerned and must be approved before the cutover.
Prepare the list of addresses to add, account by account.
Once the domain is verified in the target, add each address as a secondary address, in lower case, without touching the primary address.
steps.where: On-premises Active Directory of the target

steps.text: Run a sync, then carry on with the cutover.

configuration.target: Source addresses added as smtp: (lower case)
configuration.where: On-premises Active Directory of the target

verification: Get-Mailbox -Identity '<account upn>' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty EmailAddresses shows the added addresses.
A message sent to the old address lands in the target mailbox.
risks: An address whose domain is not yet verified in the target is ignored. Wait for verification.
Do not replace the primary address (SMTP: in upper case) without a decision from the customer.

links.title: Cloud management of Exchange attributes in a hybrid environment
Add or remove email addresses for a mailbox in Exchange Online

procedures.title: Add and verify the domain in the target, then turn on mail
procedures.goal: The domain is verified in the target, with the Email and OfficeCommunicationsOnline services active.
procedures.duration: 30 min per domain, plus propagation time
prerequisites: The domain has been removed from the source.
Access to the DNS host of the domain.
A Microsoft Graph PowerShell connection to the target with the right to manage domains.

steps.text: Add the domain to the target.
steps.where: Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Domains > Add domain, or Microsoft Graph PowerShell

steps.text: Read the MS=... TXT value specific to the domain.
Publish this TXT record at the domain root with a TTL of 300 s.
steps.where: DNS host console of the domain

steps.text: Verify the domain once the TXT record is visible.
Turn on mail and Teams for the domain.
Check that the domain shows as an accepted domain in Exchange Online.
Repeat for each domain.

configuration.target: MS=ms... (the value read in the target, specific to the domain)

verification: Get-MgDomain -DomainId <domain> | Format-List Id,IsVerified,SupportedServices shows IsVerified True, with Email.
Resolve-DnsName -Name <domain> -Type TXT -Server 1.1.1.1 -DnsOnly shows the published MS=... value.
Get-AcceptedDomain lists the domain.
risks: Adding the domain fails as long as it exists in the source, and removal can take up to a day.
Verification often takes about ten minutes, sometimes more depending on the host.
If the target is hybrid and migrated accounts are synced from on-premises Active Directory, the UPN suffix and the addresses must also be handled on-premises.

links.title: Add a custom domain to Microsoft 365
Gather the information you need to create DNS records

procedures.title: Reproduce the calling settings of users
procedures.goal: The forwards, delegations and call groups of users are reproduced in the target, or the users are warned.
prerequisites: Numbers are assigned to the target accounts.
Delegates and forwarding targets exist in the target.

steps.text: Record the settings of each user before the cutover.
Reproduce the call forward.
Reproduce the handling of unanswered calls.
Reproduce each delegation, with the rights recorded in the source. All five rights are required.
Reproduce the call groups, or warn the user to redo them in Teams.
steps.where: Teams client > Settings > Calls; communication to users

configuration.target: A number or account that exists after the cutover

verification: Get-CsUserCallingSettings -Identity <account> shows the forward, unanswered handling, groups and delegates.
risks: A target left on a number or account of the source makes the forward fail.
These settings belong to the user. Warn them before changing them.

links.title: Configure call forwarding and delegation settings

procedures.title: Recreate dial plans and voice routing
procedures.goal: The dial plans, voice routes and routing policies needed exist in the target and are assigned to the migrated voice users.
prerequisites: The provider decision is made.
The voice configuration of the source is recorded.
The existing rules of the target are recorded, to avoid name conflicts.

steps.text: Record the plans, routes and policies of the source and the target.
steps.command:
Get-CsTenantDialPlan | Format-List Identity,NormalizationRules
Get-CsOnlineVoiceRoute | Format-Table Identity,NumberPattern,OnlinePstnGatewayList,OnlinePstnUsages
Get-CsOnlineVoiceRoutingPolicy | Format-Table Identity,OnlinePstnUsages
Get-CsOnlinePstnUsage | Format-List Usage

steps.text: Create the dial plan and its normalization rule.
steps.where: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell, target tenant; Teams admin center > Voice > Dial plans

steps.text: With Direct Routing, add the PSTN usage.
Create the voice route.
Create the routing policy.
Assign the dial plan to the migrated voice users.
Assign the routing policy to the same users.

configuration.target: No conflict with those of the target

verification: Get-CsOnlineUser -Identity <account> | Format-List DisplayName,TenantDialPlan,OnlineVoiceRoutingPolicy shows the assignments.
risks: A route in the wrong order can send calls to the wrong gateway.
A rule that is too broad can change the dialing of users already in the target.
Routing policies only apply to Direct Routing.

links.title: Configure call routing for Direct Routing

procedures.title: Recreate the emergency addresses in the target
procedures.goal: The emergency addresses and places are created and validated in the target before the numbers arrive.
prerequisites: The addresses and places of the source are recorded.
The customer confirmed the civic addresses.

steps.text: Record the addresses and places of the source.
Confirm each address with the customer, including the floor or room.
Create the address in the target.
steps.where: Teams admin center > Locations > Emergency addresses; MicrosoftTeams PowerShell

steps.text: Add the useful places to this address.
Note the ID of each location for the number assignment.

verification: Get-CsOnlineLisCivicAddress, run in the target, shows the addresses.
Get-CsOnlineLisLocation -CivicAddressId <address id> | Format-Table Location,LocationId shows the places.
risks: A wrong address can send emergency services to the wrong place.
How locations are managed varies with the connection: Calling Plan, Operator Connect or Direct Routing.
Without a validated location, assigning a number can fail.

procedures.title: Move the phone numbers to the target
procedures.goal: The numbers of the source move to the target on a known date, with no unplanned outage.
procedures.duration: 2 days of effort over at least 10 business days
prerequisites: The customer has decided the number provider.
Teams Phone licenses and Calling Plans are available in the target before the date.
Emergency addresses are created and validated in the target.
Resource accounts are recreated.

steps.text: List the numbers, their type and their assignment.
Choose the path by type. Microsoft Calling Plan: no direct move between tenants, go through the Microsoft number service or a port. Other types: go through the provider.
Gather the porting documents: the authorization letter and the account details of the current provider.
File the request at least 10 business days before the date. Choose a weekday.
steps.where: Teams admin center > Voice > Phone numbers, target tenant, or the provider

steps.text: On the planned day, remove the number from the source account, if the provider or Microsoft asks for it.
Once the number is received, assign it to the target account, with its emergency location.
Test an inbound and an outbound call per pilot account, then for each attendant.

configuration.target: At least 10 business days, on a weekday
CallingPlan, OperatorConnect or DirectRouting, as decided

verification: Get-CsPhoneNumberAssignment -TelephoneNumber <number> | Format-List TelephoneNumber,NumberType,AssignedPstnTargetId,LocationId shows the assignment.
Get-CsOnlineUser -Identity <account> | Format-List DisplayName,LineUri,EnterpriseVoiceEnabled shows the number.
risks: An error in the account name or address can get the port refused and move the date.
The current provider confirms a port, and its answer can take several business days.
A partial port can affect the remaining numbers of the account. Validate it with the provider.
The move is not aligned with the mail cutover. Plan it apart.

procedures.title: Decide the telephony provider of migrated numbers
procedures.goal: The customer has decided whether the numbers of the sources join the provider of the target or keep their current provider.
prerequisites: The current routing of the target is documented.
The contract of the target's provider is known.
The list of numbers of the sources and their type.

steps.text: Confirm how the target connects: Direct Routing or Operator Connect.
steps.command:
Get-CsOnlinePSTNGateway | Format-Table Identity,Enabled
Get-CsOnlineVoiceRoute | Format-Table Identity,NumberPattern,OnlinePstnGatewayList,OnlinePstnUsages
Get-CsOnlineVoiceRoutingPolicy | Format-Table Identity,OnlinePstnUsages

steps.text: Check with the target's provider that it can take these numbers.
Present both options to the customer: port to this provider, or keep the current one.
Record the decision in the single telephony plan.
Then align the dial plans and routing.
steps.where: Teams admin center > Voice, target tenant

verification: The telephony plan holds the customer's decision.
risks: A late decision blocks the porting, the licenses and the dial plans.
Keeping a second provider adds a route to maintain in the target.

links.title: Configure call routing for Direct Routing

procedures.title: Export and recreate schedules and holidays
procedures.goal: The schedules and holiday calendars of the source are available in the target for the attendants.
prerequisites: The list of attendants of the source and their IDs.
The MicrosoftTeams module is connected to the source and the target.

steps.text: List the schedules and the attendants that use them.
steps.command:
Get-CsOnlineSchedule | Format-Table Name,Id,Type
Get-CsAutoAttendant -Identity <attendant id> | Format-List Name,Schedules,CallHandlingAssociations

steps.text: Export the holidays of each attendant.
Have the customer validate the future dates.
Recreate the opening hours before the attendants. Holidays are created in the admin center.
If the target attendant already exists, import the holiday file instead.

configuration.target: A value reviewed for each site

verification: Get-CsOnlineSchedule | Format-Table Name,Id,Type, run in the target, shows the schedules.
risks: The import needs an attendant that already exists, so choose one method per attendant.
An expired calendar sends callers to the wrong greeting.
Keep the exported files: the source disappears at closure.

procedures.title: Prepare licenses and assignments of voice users
procedures.goal: The voice users and resource accounts of the source have their license and voice configuration in the target when telephony cuts over.
prerequisites: The list of voice users is validated.
Teams Phone licenses are ordered.
The provider decision is made.

steps.text: List the voice users and match them with the matrix.
Confirm the need for Teams Phone licenses and, if any, Calling Plans.
Assign the licenses to the target accounts.
steps.where: Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Licenses, target tenant

steps.text: When telephony cuts over, turn voice on and assign the number.
Assign the dial plan and routing, then the calling policy.
Test on a pilot group before the other users.

configuration.target: Teams Phone, and a Calling Plan if any

verification: Get-CsOnlineUser -Identity <account> | Format-List EnterpriseVoiceEnabled,LineUri,TenantDialPlan,OnlineVoiceRoutingPolicy,TeamsCallingPolicy shows the expected values.
risks: With no license in the target, the number cannot be assigned on the move day.
License purchase time can delay all of telephony. Track it from now on.

procedures.title: Recreate auto attendants, call queues and resource accounts
procedures.goal: The auto attendants, call queues and resource accounts of the source work in the target.
prerequisites: Agents already exist in the target.
Microsoft Teams Phone Resource Account licenses are available.
Schedules and holidays are exported.
Audio files are recovered.

steps.text: Document each attendant, queue and resource account.
steps.command:
Get-CsAutoAttendant | Format-Table Name,Identity,LanguageId,TimeZoneId
Get-CsCallQueue | Format-Table Name,Identity,RoutingMethod
Get-CsOnlineApplicationInstance | Format-Table DisplayName,UserPrincipalName,ApplicationId,PhoneNumber

steps.text: Export the audio files of each attendant (ApplicationId OrgAutoAttendant) and each queue (HuntGroup).
Create the resource account of an attendant. For a queue, use ApplicationId 11cd3e2e-fccb-42ad-ad00-878b93575e07.
Assign the Microsoft Teams Phone Resource Account license to each resource account.
steps.where: Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Licenses, target tenant

steps.text: Create the queues before the attendants, so calls can be routed to them. Complete the agents and options in the admin center.
steps.where: Teams admin center > Voice > Call queues; MicrosoftTeams PowerShell

steps.text: Create the auto attendants in the admin center: greeting, menus, hours and holidays.
steps.where: Teams admin center > Voice > Auto attendants

steps.text: Associate each resource account with its attendant or queue. Use CallQueue for a queue.
Assign the number to the resource account once it is received, then call each attendant.

verification: Each attendant answers a test call.
The read commands of step 1, run in the target, show the expected objects.
risks: An attendant does not copy between tenants. It must be recreated.
Resource accounts have sign-in disabled and must stay that way.
A queue with no agent in the target receives no call. Create the accounts first.
Review the time zones of the attendants: Microsoft changes some regions over time.

procedures.title: Validate how private and shared channels are handled
procedures.goal: The handling of private and shared channels is validated during the pilot, and B2B direct connect is ready if they are shared with other organizations.
prerequisites: The list of private and shared channels of each team.
The copy tool is in pilot.
The tenant ID of each external organization concerned.

steps.text: List the channels by team, then note the external members.
steps.command:
Get-TeamChannel -GroupId <team id> -MembershipType Shared | Format-Table DisplayName,Id
Get-TeamChannel -GroupId <team id> -MembershipType Private | Format-Table DisplayName,Id

steps.text: Test during the pilot the copy of a shared channel: structure, members, files and messages.
Record what the tool does not carry over, and plan to recreate it by hand.
For a channel shared with another organization, add it and allow B2B direct connect, inbound and outbound.
steps.where: Microsoft Entra admin center > External Identities > Cross-tenant access settings > Organizational settings

steps.text: Have the same configuration done at the other organization: both sides are required.
Confirm that the channel policy of the target allows external sharing.
steps.where: Teams admin center > Teams > Channels policies

configuration.target: Allowed for each partner organization, inbound and outbound

verification: Get-MgPolicyCrossTenantAccessPolicyPartner | Format-Table TenantId shows the configured organizations.
risks: B2B direct connect is blocked by default, inbound and outbound.
Microsoft Entra guests cannot be added to a shared channel.
A channel shared with another organization needs action from its administrator. Plan the delay.

procedures.title: Validate and re-invite team guests
procedures.goal: The guests still useful are confirmed by the owners, then added to the teams of the target after the copy.
prerequisites: The team copy is finished.
Team owners can be reached.
Guest access is allowed in the target.

steps.text: List the guests of each team.
steps.command: Get-TeamUser -GroupId <team id> | Where-Object Role -eq 'guest' | Format-Table User,Name,Role

steps.text: Have the owners validate the list.
Invite each validated guest to the target.
Add the guest to the group of the copied team: Microsoft does not support adding a guest to a team with an application permission.
Warn the guest: they change organization in Teams.

verification: Get-TeamUser -GroupId <team id> | Where-Object Role -eq 'guest', run in the target, shows the guests.
Get-MgUser -Filter "userType eq 'Guest'" -All | Format-Table DisplayName,Mail shows the invited guests.
risks: A guest of the source keeps no access in the target: they must be invited again.
An invitation that is not accepted leaves the guest with no access.
A cross-tenant guest can already exist in the target.

procedures.title: Name two owners per team
procedures.goal: Each team has at least two owners before the copy.
prerequisites: The list of teams with one owner or none.
A person at the customer names the owners.

steps.text: List the owners of each team.
steps.command: Get-Team | ForEach-Object { [pscustomobject]@{ Team = $_.DisplayName; Owners = @(Get-TeamUser -GroupId $_.GroupId -Role Owner).Count } } | Where-Object Owners -lt 2

steps.text: Ask the customer to name the missing owners.
Add each owner, before the copy.
Carry the mapping into the copy plan, so that owners follow in the target.

verification: The command of step 1 returns no team.
risks: A team with no owner has nobody to validate guests or access.
An owner excluded from the migration leaves the team orphaned in the target.

procedures.title: Apply a single set of Teams policies
procedures.goal: Migrated accounts receive the Teams policies of the target or a recreated policy, assigned by group.
prerequisites: The list of custom policies of each source.
The customer's answer: policies of the target or policies specific to the business unit.
Assignment groups by business unit exist.

steps.text: Compare each source policy with that of the target.
steps.command:
Get-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy | Format-Table Identity
Get-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy | Format-Table Identity
Get-CsTeamsCallingPolicy | Format-Table Identity

steps.text: Decide for each policy: apply the one of the target, or recreate it.
Create in the target the policies to recreate. Aim for one policy per user profile, not one per source.
Assign the policy to the group of the business unit, with a rank.
Check the effective policy on a pilot account of each unit.

verification: Get-CsGroupPolicyAssignment -PolicyType TeamsMeetingPolicy | Format-Table GroupId,PolicyName,Rank shows the assignments.
risks: A direct assignment takes priority over a group assignment.
A user in several groups receives the policy with the best rank.
A capability taken away must be announced to users.
